correctness.rationale: Under the one-color-per-positive-vertex rule, a colored hub forces the positive rim support to dominate the cycle, giving k=ceil(n/3) as its attainable minimum size. A zero hub forces independent rim zeros and at least ceil(n/2) positive rim positions; for n≥9 the only non-strict comparison with 1+k is at n=10, where five alternating positive positions would have to alternate colors around an odd cycle. For a fixed hub color, if p rim positions carry the other color, then n−k≤2p. Only n≡1 mod 3 can have p<k; there p=k−1 and coverage is exact. Every gap of other-color vertices then contains exactly two zeros, with the lone same-color vertex between the two zeros in a unique gap. Its fixed rim index gives exactly n choices. In the all-opposite-color case each gap has length 0,1,2, and marking one selected vertex counts each support k times. Thus the counts for one hub color are (n/k)[u^(n−k)](1+u+u²)^k, plus n when n≡1 mod 3. Evaluating the three coefficients and doubling gives 6, n(n+11)/3, and 2n in the stated order. An independent direct census for n=9,10,11,12 returned counts 6,70,22,6 with no zero-hub minimizer; this only corroborates the proof. The supplied verify.py was inspected, not executed.
